summary: Console metrics disappeared for subset of org routes after tenant schema migration
description:
Issue summary:
Customer OptimaDocs reports that after a scheduled tenant schema migration we performed on 2026-03-09, several dashboard widgets and the Console usage rollups for some of their org routes display zero or drastically lower metrics. Raw event ingestion appears intact (we can see individual request logs and traces), but aggregated counts and heatmaps are missing for specific route prefixes (org/optima/*).

Impact:
- Multiple dashboards for OptimaDocs show empty time series for the 2026-03-09 00:00 - 2026-03-10 12:00 window.
- Alerts tied to rollup thresholds did not fire correctly, causing a delayed detection of a throughput regression.
- Customer-facing analytics in Console are unreliable for the affected routes; this impacts billing visibility and product monitoring.

Environment:
- prod-us-east, tenant migration job run 2026-03-09 03:42 UTC.
- Affected tenant: org-id optima-2042.

Steps to reproduce (support verified):
1) Login to Console as customer (optima-2042) and open the traffic overview dashboard.
2) Filter by route prefix org/optima/documents.* between 2026-03-09 00:00 and 2026-03-10 12:00.
3) Observe that panel 'Requests per minute by route' shows a flat zero series; traces and raw logs for same times exist in trace explorer.

Observed behavior:
- Aggregation queries hitting the analytics-backend return empty result sets for the affected org_alias.
- Querying raw events by org_id returns matching records (sample log ids: req-20260309-9a1b, req-20260309-9a2c).
- Console rollup index name used in aggregation appears to be the pre-migration alias for some shards, resulting in a mismatch.

Expected behavior:
- Dashboard panels and rollups should reflect aggregated counts based on raw events regardless of background migration, or fall back gracefully with a clear notice if a migration is in-progress.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- We advised OptimaDocs to view raw events/trace explorer for immediate debugging.
- Support created an alias redirect on the query layer (internal workaround) to point aggregation queries at the correct post-migration index; this restores panel results for most widgets while a permanent fix is prepared.

Additional context and evidence:
- Sample raw event: {timestamp: "2026-03-09T03:45:12Z", org_id: "optima-2042", route: "org/optima/documents/upload", request_id: "req-20260309-9a1b"} (present in raw logs but missing from hourly rollups).
- Aggregation query (anonymized) returned HTTP 200 with empty buckets for the affected time range.
- Migration job log excerpt: "migration: tenant-mapping update applied for optima-2042, aliases rotated 03:42 UTC" (see Confluence runbook link).

2026-03-09T03:42:45Z alias-rotator INFO rotated index aliases: metrics-rollup-v23 -> metrics-rollup-v24
2026-03-09T03:45:12Z ingest-proxy INFO received request id=req-20260309-9a1b org=optima-2042 route=org/optima/documents/upload
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:10 - Support: Confirmed raw events and traces exist for affected time window; aggregation returns empty buckets for specific org_alias.

2026-03-10 11:23 - SRE: Reproduced locally against a staging snapshot; observed that aggregation service queries an alias resolved to v23 indexes while the rollups were written to v24 during migration overlap.

2026-03-10 13:00 - DataEng hypothesis: race condition in alias-rotation script where some routing keys retained old alias; aggregation backend caches resolved alias for 6h by default and did not refresh after rotation.

2026-03-11 02:14 - Engineering: Cache invalidation path confirmed; aggregation client does not detect index alias change when a mapping version bump occurs, leading to zero results until cache TTL expires or manual invalidation occurs.
2026-03-12 18:40 - Patch created to add alias-change event hook to aggregation client and to proactively invalidate cache on migration completion (PR linked).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Assigned to SRE for immediate triage and requested escalation due to billing impact.
2026-03-10 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Reproduced in staging. Placing temporary query alias redirect for optima-2042. Notifying DataEng for root cause. #support-optima
2026-03-11 - OptimaDocs (customer): Thank you — dashboards are returning data after your workaround. Can you confirm whether historical rollups will be repaired?

2026-03-12 - DataEng (Elena Morales): We will run a backfill to re-aggregate the missed windows to metrics-rollup-v24. Backfill ETA: 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC. Post-backfill we will run validation scripts and merge aliases cleanly.
2026-03-14 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Backfill started at 2026-03-14 04:12 UTC (job id backfill-867530). Monitoring progress; will update when complete.
resolution_summary: (pending) Temporary alias redirect restored dashboard visibility; root cause is aggregation-client cache not invalidating after index alias rotation during tenant schema migration. Fix implemented in PR to add alias-change hooks and reduce cache TTL; backfill scheduled to regenerate missing hourly rollups for optima-2042. Final resolution will be updated after backfill completes and validation passes.
resolution_notes: Change merged: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1284 - add alias-change event hook to aggregation client and proactive cache invalidation
Post-backfill validation steps: compare hourly rollup totals against raw event counts; run dashboard smoke tests for OptimaDocs org routes.
Follow-up: Add a migration-run checklist to the runbook to remove in-flight cache TTLs prior to alias rotation (Confluence updated).
followup_actions: Deploy aggregation-client fix to prod (rollout window 2026-03-15 02:00 - 05:00 UTC).
Complete backfill and confirm dashboards restored for optima-2042; mark ticket resolved after validation.
Update migration runbook to include cache invalidation steps and add health-check to detect alias mismatch immediately after migration.
